clue.text: One taking a buckshee voyage has to pack

definitions.meaning: someone who hides aboard a ship to travel without paying the fare
a verb phrase: to put cargo or luggage neatly away in a hold

explanation.surface: Someone sailing for free is obliged to do the packing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buckshee' is British slang for free of charge. The first sense is a noun and the second a verb phrase, with 'has' only joining them.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun naming a ship's hidden free traveller, and the two-word verb for storing things out of sight.

clue.text: Subject other people to the ultimate in impertinence

parts.note: them is the pronoun for other people

indicators.note: the ultimate in a word is its final letter, so take the end of impertinence

explanation.surface: Someone subjects others to the height of rudeness.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject of a talk or essay, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Chest of drawers could be so described-and something more

definitions.text: Chest of drawers could be so described
definitions.meaning: a literal description of furniture whose drawers have handles fitted
an informal British idiom meaning even more so, to a greater degree

explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom 'with knobs on' means 'and then some', often said to return an insult with interest.
explanation.definitionFit: A chest with handles literally has them fitted, and the idiom itself means even more so.

clue.text: Soak is good for nothing in battle

indicators.note: good for nothing says one letter standing for good takes the place of the one standing for nothing

parts.note: Waterloo, the 1815 battle where Napoleon was defeated
O is the round figure meaning nothing

explanation.surface: A drunkard proves useless on the battlefield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good for nothing' looks like an insult; it says swap the O of WATERLOO for G. 'Soak' is a noun (a drunk) in the surface but the verb in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To waterlog something is to saturate it with water, so it means to soak thoroughly.

clue.text: Let one's work get replaced with play here

indicators.note: read as re-placed, the letters are put back in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe dropped
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Somewhere you can forget the office and take a holiday instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get replaced with play' reads as swapping work for leisure, but it adds PLAY to LET ONE'S WORK and rearranges the lot. The definition 'here' points to the place the whole clue describes, a famous US national park.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue paints a holiday spot, and this American national park is a place where people go to play.

clue.text: To speak contemptuously can cause alarm

parts.note: diss (also dis) is slang for to insult or disparage
may means can, as in permission

explanation.surface: Talking down to people may frighten them.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismay someone is to fill them with consternation, which is to cause alarm.

clue.text: Magistrate imprisons soldiers showing decrepitude

indicators.note: one thing holding another inside it, as a jail holds a prisoner

parts.note: the Doge was the chief magistrate of Venice or Genoa
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers

explanation.surface: A judge jails some troops who look worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotage is the feebleness of old age, a synonym for decrepitude.

clue.text: Gentleman is retired, right?

indicators.note: something retired has gone back, so the word is is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a gentleman has stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir is the polite form of address for a gentleman.

clue.text: Real changes at uni/tech

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Genuine reforms are happening at a technical university.
explanation.definitionFit: Authentic and real both mean genuine, not fake.

clue.text: Go away and get busy

definitions.meaning: a slang command to leave at once
read as three words, to ... is to be busily working

explanation.surface: Someone is told to clear off and do some work.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the answer as BE AT IT, to be hard at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A curt slang order to leave, and also, split into three words, an instruction to be working hard.

clue.text: Learned to use repetition, following lecturer's lead

indicators.note: the repetition piece comes after the lecturer's lead letter
a word's lead is its leading, first letter

parts.note: to iterate is to repeat

explanation.surface: Someone learnt by rote, copying what the lecturer did first.
explanation.definitionFit: Literate means well read or educated, an adjective sense of learned.

clue.text: Part of record player fell to floor

definitions.meaning: the turntable unit of a hi-fi is called a ...
as a verb, to knock someone down with a punch

explanation.surface: A piece of the turntable dropped onto the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A record deck is the playing unit, and to deck someone is to floor them with a blow.

clue.text: Ordered in, Roger got 23

definitions.note: a cross-reference to the answer at 23-down, a word for a seasoning

indicators.note: the letters are put in order, rearranged

explanation.surface: Roger ordered a takeaway and got curry.
explanation.definitionFit: The root of the ginger plant is a spice used in cooking.

clue.text: Talks about male amphibians

indicators.note: the talking piece goes around the male piece

parts.note: natters means chats idly
a jack is a male of certain animals, such as a donkey

explanation.surface: Gossip concerning male frogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Natterjacks are a species of European toad, which are amphibians.

clue.text: Gold ring found in compost — that's funny

indicators.note: these pieces are found inside the compost word

parts.note: humus is decayed organic matter in soil
or is gold in heraldry
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Discovering a gold ring in the compost heap would be amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: Humorous and funny are synonyms, both meaning amusing.

clue.text: He couldn't possibly appear in the nude

indicators.note: the letters could be possibly rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A man insists he could never be seen naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclothed means naked, the same as in the nude.

clue.text: Some phototelegraphy could be used to convey …

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the long word are taken

explanation.surface: Part of a photo sent by wire could be used to get a message across.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry, a synonym of convey.

clue.text: Chamber often gets this official statement

definitions.meaning: read as two words, the chamber of a gun often has a ... it

explanation.surface: Parliament often receives a formal announcement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chamber' suggests a legislature; it is a gun's chamber, which often gets a BULLET IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief public news announcement from an authority is an official statement.

clue.text: … sketches in a book

definitions.meaning: short performances, turns on a stage
the ... of the Apostles, a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: Drawings appear in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Short stage turns, and the fifth book of the New Testament.

clue.text: Wealth? At one point cry, being overcome, …

indicators.note: the crying piece is overcome, surrounded by the time piece

parts.note: once means at one point in time
to pule is to whimper or cry weakly

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether riches once made them weep.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulence is great wealth and luxury.

clue.text: Secret police's period of inactivity

definitions.meaning: belonging to the Stasi, East Germany's secret police
a state of stagnation or equilibrium

explanation.surface: The secret police had a spell of doing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A possessive of the East German security service, and a word for a state of stagnation.

clue.text: … done with wealth, ruined, impoverished

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, the letters broken and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone finished with riches is left ruined and poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Down-at-heel describes someone shabby and poor, like shoes worn at the heel.

clue.text: Recently getting stick out, to lash son

indicators.note: to lash is to bind, so the protruding piece is tied around the son

parts.note: to jut is to project or stick out

explanation.surface: Someone recently pulled out a stick to whip their son.
explanation.definitionFit: Just means only a short time ago, as in just arrived, so recently.

clue.text: Groom holding pony's head getting a kick

indicators.note: the groom piece holds the other letter inside it

parts.note: sice (or syce) is an Indian word for a groom who tends horses

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A stable lad gripping a pony's head gets kicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Spice means zest or excitement, which is what a kick gives a dish or experience.

clue.text: Cleaner, one's mother shows attractive personality

parts.note: a char is a British word for a cleaning lady
I is one, and the 's gives S
ma is mother

explanation.surface: The cleaning lady's mum has great charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is a compelling charm that inspires devotion in others.

clue.text: A line read out in letter

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the word sounds like the one entered

parts.note: a row is a line of things

explanation.surface: A line read aloud within a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rho is the seventeenth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Caledonian jumps back in alarm

indicators.note: the Scottish piece turns round, read backwards

parts.note: Caledonia is the Latin name for Scotland, so a Caledonian is a Scot

explanation.surface: A Scotsman leaps backwards in fright.
explanation.definitionFit: A tocsin is an alarm bell or warning signal.

clue.text: Being overdrawn, notes in lieu of payment are repugnant

parts.note: OD is the bank abbreviation for overdrawn
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: Writing IOUs when your account is overdrawn is disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious and repugnant both mean hateful or offensive.

clue.text: Author's books left you taken aback

definitions.note: read as Author is, the definition followed by a link

parts.note: Kings is the name of two books of the Old Testament

indicators.note: aback means backwards, so the you word is turned round

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: A writer's novels leave the reader startled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' looks like surprise; it reverses YE.
explanation.definitionFit: Kingsley is the name of several British authors, notably Charles Kingsley and Kingsley Amis.
